claim: The Israeli room count includes the living room: '4 rooms' = a living room and 3 bedrooms; a '1-room' unit is a studio.
write_as: Explain once for a foreign reader; never convert to bedrooms in a table.

claim: A dunam (the Israeli land unit) is 1,000 m2.
write_as: Allowed once, to explain the unit. No other conversions (no sq ft, no acres, no hectares, no dollars or euros).

claim: Quarters: 'the first quarter of 2026' = January to March 2026 (Q1, 1-3.2026).
write_as: 'Q1 2026' or 'the first quarter of 2026'. Keep the year.

claim: The Sde Dov quarter (rova), on the site of the former airfield in north-west Tel Aviv-Yafo, is planned for about 16,000 apartments ('16 thousand') in three compounds: Eshkol (south-east), the Centre and the North.
conflict: '15,000-20,000 units' (an English guide) is not the plan: never use it.
write_as: 'about 16,000 apartments planned'. Never a delivery date for the whole quarter.

claim: A survey of the developers' annual reports published in April 2026: about 1,280 apartments sold in the quarter so far; their average price about ₪83,000 per m2; a 4-room apartment sold for about ₪9.45 million on average.
conflict: An older page figure 'about 81,000' and an average 'about 7 million per deal' have no source: never use them.
write_as: 'about ₪83,000 per m2' (an average of sold units, not an asking price).

claim: In 2026 most projects in the quarter sell at about ₪70,000 per m2.
Per the developers' 2025 reports, the sales averages of the projects in the Eshkol compound ranged from about ₪63,400 to about ₪82,600 per m2, VAT included.
The largest deal published in the quarter: an apartment of about 390 m2 with a balcony of about 200 m2 on floor 38 of a tower in the Central compound, sold in December 2025 for more than ₪42 million.
conflict: '43.75 million for 508 m2' had no source: never use it.
write_as: 'more than ₪42 million'.

claim: Sde Dov (Dov Hoz airport) was inaugurated on 23 September 1938, with the Tel Aviv - Haifa - Beirut air line; it closed on 1 July 2019 and its evacuation was completed early in 2020.
conflict: Some English sources say 30 June 2019 (the last day of flights): write 1 July 2019, as the Hebrew does.
write_as: The city is Tel Aviv; the line name keeps the three cities.

claim: The quarter covers about 1,300 dunam along the sea in north Tel Aviv; its coastal front (the coastal park) is about 2 km long.
conflict: '1,500 dunam' (also 1,490 / 1,600 in some press and marketing) has no official basis: never use it.
write_as: 'about 1,300 dunam'. 'about 1.3 km2' is NOT allowed (a new number).

claim: Boundaries: the Tzukei Aviv neighbourhood and Propes Street (north); Neve Yam, Plan L (Tochnit Lamed) and Levi Eshkol Street (east); Kochav HaTzafon, the Reading compound and Shai Agnon Street (south); the beach and the promenade (west).
write_as: No distances. The port of Tel Aviv is NOT a boundary.

claim: The master plan describes a mixed-use quarter of about 16,000 apartments for about 40,000 residents; it came into force in August 2020.
write_as: 'about 40,000 residents' (41,000 appears in some press: never use it).

claim: Per the plan approved in 2020: about 500,000 m2 of public buildings, about 125,000 m2 of hotels and about 365 dunam of parks and public gardens; of the 16,000 apartments about 2,400 are for affordable housing at a reduced price and about 4,500 for special housing (student dormitories, assisted living, rental housing).
conflict: '4,500 to 6,900 special-housing units' misreads the source (6,900 = 2,400 + 4,500): never write 6,900.

claim: The three compounds: Eshkol (TAMAL/3001) about 4,800 apartments, about 45,000 m2 of commerce, about 145,000 m2 of employment; the Centre about 7,100 apartments (7,128 in the approved plan), about 60,000 m2 of commerce, about 155,000 m2 of employment and about 800 hotel rooms; the North about 4,000 apartments, about 20,000 m2 of commerce, about 30,000 m2 of employment and about 1,150 hotel rooms. No separate hotel figure for Eshkol.
write_as: The Eshkol hotel cell stays without a number.

claim: Dates in force: the master plan August 2020; the Eshkol detailed plan May 2021; the Centre and North detailed plans 2025.
conflict: 'Eshkol preceded the master plan' is wrong: never write it.

claim: In February and March 2025, eight land tenders closed for 6,666 apartments, more than 40% of the apartments planned in the quarter.
write_as: 'eight tenders' in words or 8; never 41.7% (not in the Hebrew).

claim: Rainbow Tel Aviv (Israel Canada, Eshkol compound): a tower of 39 to 40 floors and boutique buildings; 459 apartments per the developer (the land tender spoke of 480); the main contractor Ashtrom was chosen in January 2026; delivery in stages, the last stage expected in 2030.
conflict: '480 per marketing / 459 per permit' were wrong attributions: never use them.
write_as: 2030 is the expected last stage, not a contractual date.

claim: Project facts (as the area map cards): FIRST, a 45-floor tower and three boutique buildings of 9 floors, 350 apartments; ASHIRA, 406 apartments in four buildings including a 35-floor tower; DIMRI YAMA, 458 apartments in a 40-floor tower, a 16-floor mid-rise (towerlet) and two 9-floor buildings; ZOHI, about 230 apartments; GINDI VOGUE, 708 apartments on two lots in the Centre, including a 45-floor tower and three 20-floor towers; UTOPIA, 337 apartments in four buildings around a shared courtyard in Eshkol.
write_as: Only if the Hebrew row carries it (the six table cells are optional edits).

claim: Rainbow Tel Aviv: the average of all apartments sold up to March 2026 was about ₪81,800 per m2.
conflict: 'about 82,000' was the rounded, undated form: use 81,800 with its date.

claim: At these prices (about ₪70,000 to ₪83,000 per m2) a 100 m2 apartment costs about ₪7 to ₪8.3 million (a calculation, as the price calculator on the prices page).
conflict: 'a 100 m2 apartment about 8 million' was 100 x an unsourced 80,000: never use it.
write_as: Say it is a calculation.

claim: Land prices in the tenders: about ₪3.3 million per apartment on average in the 2022 tenders (development costs included); about ₪1.7 to ₪2.2 million per apartment in the February 2025 tender for regular (for-sale) apartment buildings (the rental tenders of that month were far lower).
conflict: 'over 3 million per unit' without a year: never use it.

claim: Luxury deals of ₪14 million and more have been published in the quarter (since 10.2024).
Public participation: five meetings during the master plan; four topic meetings for the detailed plans (traffic and transport; building and urban design; building and programme; housing).
write_as: Words or digits.

claim: 'In a new neighbourhood you buy the apartment and also the first ten years of the neighbourhood being built around it' (the page's own line).
The page was checked and updated in October 2026 (7.10.2026).
write_as: Only in the Hebrew page; the translations carry no date line.

claim: In December 2025 three apartments on floors 38, 39 and 43 of a tower facing the sea sold for about ₪107,700 to ₪119,200 per m2 of built area (balconies not counted).
March 2026: two deals for 5-room apartments of 132 m2 on floor 9 in one project, ₪7.16 to ₪7.57 million, about ₪54,200 to ₪57,300 per m2 ('deals of 54,000-57,000 per m2').
The range of deals in the April 2026 survey: about ₪60,200 to ₪138,000 per m2.
Tel Aviv-Yafo: the median of deals in the two years to October 2025 (October 2023 to October 2025) was ₪52,856 per m2.
source: TA (Tax Authority deals; the site's Tel Aviv card)
write_as: A median of deals, not an average.

claim: In one project in the quarter the average rose from about ₪64,700 per m2 in the first quarter of 2026 to about ₪81,600 per m2 in the eight deals after it (VAT included).
write_as: 'eight deals' (a small sample).

claim: In June 2026 one developer valued its unsold apartments at about ₪73,200 per m2 incl. VAT, below its 2025 deals average of about ₪82,500.
write_as: An estimate, not a deal.

claim: The official (list) prices in the projects: ₪75,000 to ₪85,000 per m2 before financing benefits.
write_as: List prices before financing benefits, not deals.

claim: Per one developer in the quarter (December 2025), selected apartments sold at ₪90,000 to ₪100,000 per m2.
2 rooms: recent deals in one Eshkol project ₪2.8 to ₪3.1 million (May 2026); in its presale ₪2.4 to ₪2.7 million. Another 2-room deal: 54 m2, floor 9, ₪3.665 million, about ₪67,900 per m2 (2026).
3 rooms of 82-83 m2: recent deals in the same Eshkol project ₪4.6 to ₪4.8 million (May 2026).
4-5 rooms of 104-126 m2 on floors 10-13, four deals: ₪6.49 to ₪7.73 million, about ₪61,300 to ₪62,800 per m2 (2026).
5 rooms of 139.7 m2 on floor 18 (of 20), on one project's price list: ₪11.954 million, about ₪85,600 per m2 (October 2025); in round words 'up to ₪11.95 million on one price list'.
write_as: A price-list (asking) price, not a deal.

claim: Summaries of the published deals and price lists: 2-room apartments sold in 2026 for about ₪2.8 to ₪3.7 million; 5-room apartments of 126-132 m2 sold in 2026 for about ₪7.2 to ₪7.7 million; 5 rooms in deals and price lists from about ₪7.2 to about ₪12 million; 4 and 5 rooms about ₪6.5 to ₪12 million.
write_as: Ranges as written in the Hebrew; no new averages.

claim: A 1-room apartment of 32 m2 on floor 4 of one of the towers sold in July 2023 for ₪3.1 million.
conflict: '2.3 million for 32 m2' had no source: never use it.

claim: FIRST (Hagag Group, Central compound): by July 2025, about 94 apartments plus 8 more agreements were marketed for about ₪853 million, about ₪8.4 million per apartment on average; its 2025 average about ₪75,500 per m2.
Eshkol: in one project the recent deals were at ₪60,000 to ₪62,000 per m2 (May 2026); the Centre and the North have no separate published average.
write_as: 'no separate average published'.

claim: Ramat Aviv: recent deals average about ₪55,000 per m2 (June 2026); Ramat Aviv Gimel about ₪51,000 to ₪53,000 per m2 (August 2026). Park Tzameret: depends on the tower and the floor (no figure).
conflict: 'Park Tzameret 90,000-120,000' had no source: never use it.

claim: In March 2025 the developer Yigal Dimri estimated that in a decade or two prices in the quarter could reach ₪150,000 per m2: a very optimistic forecast against today's average of about ₪83,000.
write_as: A forecast; 'a decade or two'.

claim: Counts in the page's own words: four main price factors; three markets (small apartments, family apartments, premium); at least ten parameters for comparing two apartments.
write_as: Words or digits.
